header_sentences: See Chastise, Fine, Punish, Torment, and Torture.

contexts.text: Falsity and evil have in them the penalty of falsity and evil; consequently, the fear of the penalty.
Evil returns to him who does evil, and becomes the evil of penalty... But still the Lord turns all the evil of penalty into good...

Such is the equilibrium... that the evil itself punishes itself; so that in evil there is the penalty of the evil. In like manner in falsity... Hence each person induces on himself the penalty and torment... But as the evil Spirit himself rushes into it, the Lord turns all the penalty and torment into good, and into some use; for there never can be any penalty, unless there is with the Lord an end of use... AC 1011:end.
(Such seducers) undergo a most grievous penalty in the other life. Described. SE 2708.
This penalty returns many times during hundreds and thousands of years, until they are imbued with horror for such cupidities. SE 2709.

The penalty (of those who think lasciviously) is that... they are thrown prostrate and are circumrotated... naked before all... and at the same time shame is instilled into them. Then they are revolved by the head and feet... and resistance is induced, and pain; for there are two forces acting... An opportunity is then afforded him to withdraw... but still there are some who try him to see whether he persists in such things; but so long as he is in a state of shame and pain, he is on his guard... This penalty appeared in front, at some distance. SE 1696.
(The penalty of dislocation. Described.)
All the evils and falsities of an evil man return in the other life, and are turned into infernal phantasies and penalties.

There are, besides, diverse penalties with which the evil (there) are most grievously punished, and into which they run when they return into their filthy cupidities, and by which they contract shames, terrors, and horrors for such things, until at last they desist... In general these are the penalties of laceration, of rending, of the veil...

Those tenacious of revenge, who suppose themselves greater than all others... have the penalty of laceration. Described... He is afterwards... immersed in a clayey pool... and this is done repeatedly, until such a cupidity is taken away.
(The penalty of rending, or racking. Described.)
(The penalty of the cone. Described.)

(The penalty of violent collisions of the parts backwards and forwards. Described.) Being Sirens, they tried with many arts to elude the penalty, but could not. Described. This severe penalty is necessary in order that man may sleep in safety.

By withdrawing into a more subtle nature... they suppose themselves safe from all penalty. But these, too, not only undergo the penalties of rending... but are also conglutinated... and the more they desire to be loosened from one another, the more closely they are fastened. This penalty is attended with a more intense torment, because it responds to their more hidden deceits.
Those who use the words of Scripture in jests... undergo the penalties of rending, until they desist...
There is also the penalty of rending as to the thoughts... (See SE 3179.)
(The penalty of the veil. See Punish.)
No one undergoes any penalty or torment there on account of his hereditary evil, but on account of the actual evils which he has himself perpetrated. AC 2308. HH 342:5. AE 989:end.
When the evil are being punished. Angels are always present, who regulate the penalty...
The more they would lift up their heads out of Hell... the more frightful are the penalties into which they precipitate themselves.
When evil goes beyond its limits, it runs into the penalty of the evil.
When a man does evil without penalty he supposes that the Lord does not care; and when he undergoes the penalty, he then thinks that the Lord sees; nay, that the Lord is punishing him...
The judgment or penalty itself of evil is presented in the lower and lowest things. Signified.

Such is the equilibrium there that the evil itself punishes itself, or, the evil run into the penalty of the evil, but when it has arrived at its height... When an evil man goes beyond the boundary of the evil, he then precipitates himself into the penalty... In like manner in general (Judgment). Explained.
The sword = the penalty of falsity. AC 2799:20.
He supposes that the Lord... wills the evil of the penalty, when yet He... does not will that anyone should be punished. AC 3605:3.
The penalty of profanation in Hell is most grievous.
After (seducers) have endured grievous penalties, they are associated with their like in Hell.
The penalty of (those who have a communion of wives) is horrible. They are bound together into a bundle, with a serpent wound round them...
As the cause is not in the king or judge, when a man... suffers the penalties of doing evil. AC 6071:2.
Fire = the penalty of evil.
The penalties of evils and falsities believed to come from Jehovah; when yet they are from man, and from the infernal crew with him.
The two principal penalties with the Jewish nation. Explained. AC 7456:2.
Some act by artifices and lies... Such Spirits are severely punished. Their penalty is diverse from the penalties of others, being effected by circumrotations. Described. SE 1763.
After the penalty, such are rejected to the back...
Others have been very filthy... They are obstinate, and do not desist through penalties, as do other devils...
Everyone pays the penalty of his own iniquity. Illustrated.
Anger = the penalty when they assault good and truth.
(There) evil and the penalty cohere; for as soon as an infernal Spirit does evil beyond his wont, the punishing Spirits are present... and this without advertence. AC 6559.
All things are from God; thus also the evils of penalty. Explained.
The evil in them punishes itself, according to the law; and through the evils of penalty they at last abstain from doing evils; and besides, the punishment of the evil is the protection of the good.
That penalty is imminent according to desert. Signified, Explained.
How it is with... penalties (there).

Such is the order there that evil itself has the penalty with it, so that the evil of deed is completely conjoined with the evil of penalty; that is, in the evil itself is its penalty... AC 7344:end. AC 7541. AC 7643:2.

[An evil Spirit] can be amended... only as to the exteriors, namely, through fears on account of penalties: when he has often endured them, he at last abstains... the cupidity to do evil still remaining. AC 7280:2. AC 7541:end.
When the Lord is ordinating the Heavens... evil Spirits rush more strongly into evils and falsities, and their penalties...
When the evil are being devastated, it is often given them to perceive whence they have the evils of penalty, that they may know... themselves to be the cause.
Hence the evil there undergo penalties, until at last they... do not infest the good...
The evil (thus) cast themselves into the penalty of retaliation... Signified.
Until at last such an ardour is assuaged, from fear of the penalty.

To be stoned = the penalty of falsity and of violated truth. The reason this is the penalty for those who from self-confidence ascend to the Divine in a Heaven which is above, is that then all their intelligence perishes.
What is the penalty, and what the restitution. Treated of.
A state of exemption from penalty. Signified, Explained.
A corresponding penalty to much. Signified, Explained.
A corresponding penalty to the full. Signified, Explained.
No penalty. Signified, Explained.
Forty stripes () = penalty to the full.
Lest there be the penalty of evil in doing goods as of one's self. Signified, Explained.
There, the penalty adheres to its evil, and as it were inheres in it.

The penalties in the World of Spirits are manifold. There is no respect of persons... Every evil carries its penalty with it; they are conjoined together; and therefore he who is in evil is also in the penalty of the evil. But still no one pays the penalty on account of the evils he has done in the world; but on account of the evils he does then. But it comes to the same thing. Explained.
The fear of the penalty is the only means in that (second state after death) of mastering evils... But good Spirits are never punished... because their evils do not return. Explained.

(The infernals) are ruled through fears of penalties... The penalties there are manifold, more lenient or more grievous according to the evils. For the most part... the more malignant... are able to keep the rest in compliance by means of penalties and the consequent terrors... The solo means of restraining the violence and fury of those in the Hells is the fear of the penalty. HH 581.

Evil Spirits are severely punished in the World of Spirits, in order that by the penalties they may be deterred from doing evils... Yet nothing of the penalty there is from the Lord, but is from the evil itself; for evil is so conjoined with its own penalty, that they cannot be separated. For the infernal crew desire nothing more than... to inflict penalties... and do inflict penalties on everyone who is not protected by the Lord. Therefore, when evil is done from an evil heart, as it rejects all protection by the Lord, they rush upon him... and punish him. (Explained by penalties in this world.)
After the infestations (the infernals) begin to treat cruelly (their new associate) by means of penalties...
Without the fear of a penalty... evil would rush into furies, and the whole (Hell) would be dispersed, like a kingdom on earth where there is no law, and no penalty.
That no one is reformed by means of threats and penalties, because they compel. General article.
(Thus) it is hurtful to compel men to Divine worship by threats and penalties.
The fear of civil penalties and of external ecclesiastical penalties does not close (the internal of thought). Explained.
The fear of infernal penalties does indeed invade the external of thought, but only for some moments, hours, or days...
Still, every evil is followed by its own penalty: it is as if on an evil there were inscribed its own penalty, which the wicked man pays after death.
Just retribution and penalty after death: that then the evils and falsities by which they have seduced... others will return upon them... Signified, Explained.
These are the retributions and penalties (after death) which are meant... by the torments in Hell.
The delight (of the demons) was changed into undelight, because, by means of penalties and the fear of them, they were restrained from their former delight...
The nature contracted in the world cannot be changed or expelled by means of penalties. Whenever it is expelled by them, it recurs after a short lapse of time.
Charity is exercised towards the evil by means of penalties, etc.
He would be punished after death, and this until he did not do evil for fear of the penalty.
The penalty of witches. Described.
(The penalty of the tun for the evil Spirits of Jupiter.) Explained.
On the penalty of women in especial, who lead a delicate and idle life.
On the penalty of those who want to counterfeit holy things. (Ulceration, itch, leprosy, lice.)

The Spirit who endured this penalty said that he wants to desist... but, as it inheres, he cannot... and therefore in order that he may be able to do so he was compelled by means of penalties. Such or the like penalties have now been inflicted on him ten times; I have seen him before, under the veil; but he still insists. It is now seventeen centuries that he has been such...
That same Spirit... was brought to this lake, to see the penalties of those miserable ones, and to choose one...

The representations there, as the penalties of the miserable ones, appear to be phantasies; but are actual; because those who suffer the penalties enjoy sense. They feel them; and are tortured exactly as if they were in the body...
On the penalty of whirling. Explained.
It is the penalty of those who do not say what they think...
In the other life there are never wanting kinds of penalties answering to every crime.
It is the Angels who regulate and relax the penalty, or permit it to extend, according to the pleasure of the Spirits (in revenge).
What the penalty of the horror of darkness effects. Explained.
Concerning the penalty of lasciviousness. (Revolution round a cord.) Compare SE 1694.
The penalty thus evolved itself from the offence.
Concerning the penalties of those who relate to stagnant humours in the brain.
(The penalties of those who kill men deceitfully).
Concerning the penalty of certain who are immersed as it were in deep clouds.
One of the penalties (of those who hold to the common conjunction of women and men) is that their lascivious members are burned as with fire...
(As they could not restrain themselves) shame, fear, horror, and like things, are struck into them by means of penalties... so that they can be different...
The penalty of those who are well endowed with cleverness, yet study only those things which serve for perversion to man.
This is the reason why the infernal torments (of those who are delighted) are more grievous than the infernal penalties of all other sins. See SE 2711.
That evil has the penalty in itself; in fact, that of retaliation. Explained.
What the penalties in the other life effect. Explained.

There are manifold penalties, more grievous and prolonged according to each person's nature contracted in the life of the body; but the penalties effect this: that for a period of time they inject fears, shames, horrors, for such things... But still they do not change the nature... but the penalties superadd those things by which they can be withdrawn from such evils.

There was one who supposed that infernal penalties will last to eternity... to whom it was shown that there can never be any penalty in the other life without an end... namely, that by means of the penalty and torments he may be tempered so as to be able to be in some good Society.
That evil Spirits could not live, unless they served for temptations, penalties, and the like, from which comes good. Explained.

He was told that the penalty of such things is one of retaliation; and therefore the evil Spirits dragged him to themselves, and tortured him with the like (pains that he had inflicted on others by sorcery). SE 2913.
From these (examples in nature) it is evident that the evil of penalty which they suppose to come from another, is from themselves; for there is such a response.
For their mind (is ruled by) the penalty...
(The penalty of inflation for those who are proud. Described.)
Concerning interior and other penalties.
He was told that he knew their penalty according to the laws of the earth...
I reflected upon their cruel penalty: how they treat the (Spirits of that Earth).
Their penalty is, that they wrap him up in a woollen cloth... holding in their hands the knot, and twisting it...
While the penalty of laceration was going on, angelic choirs were in the same place as the penalty...
The drunkenness of Spirits is one of the infernal penalties, but not a hard one...
(The Quaker Spirit who called himself the Holy Spirit) was revolved round an axis... into a thin plate... which is the penalty for saying that they are from eternity.

External bonds induce such a nature... that they appear as if they were upright, when yet, inwardly, they are wolves... Hence it is evident what the penalties in the other life [effect], which at last induce as it were a nature, so that the Spirit can be detained from evils.
To insidiate against man while asleep in the night is abominable; and therefore such attract a penalty to themselves.
When wickedness comes to its height, they precipitate themselves into the penalties; for... the equilibrium then perishes, and so they precipitate themselves...
Whenever a Spirit attempts to rush into greater evils than he has acquired by actuality in his life... he at once runs into the penalty. SE 4224.

He thus undergoes not one kind of penalty, but many; and whenever it occurs... he is punished with the penalty which conforms with his evil. But still there remains one kind of penalty, and consequently one Hell, which is that of His reigning evil.
Such penalties last a long time, through many years, and through many ages... and are attended with vastation... Thus he continually descends to the ultimate of his penalty.
The penalty of certain: that they are sent among the auriculars. Explained.
Concerning the penalties of those who disquiet man in his sleep. Explained.
The penalty advanced around me, to others... and all were found...
Other (Sirens) want... to derive the penalties upon the punishers...
The evil of penalty flows from order. If there were no evil of penalty, order would perish...

When they are in the penalty, they (most dexterously) substitute others... There are many such... they undergo the penalty of rending or reverberation, and are at the same time held in this, that they throw the blame upon others; nor are they liberated from the penalty until such a disposition ceases.
On the penalty of those who want to do violence to infants. (Circumgyration.)
The reason of there being a penalty (for Spirits who speak well). SE 4310.
Until... they are amended by means of penalties.

Concerning penalties. I have heard the penalties of reverberation and collision more frequently than I can relate, for hours... Wonderful to say, all who have been in fault are found; and those not in fault, although summoned and in the midst of the penalty, are not hurt by the penalty...
There was a certain new penalty, by means of a species of circumrotation of a number; thus as it were of the confounding of a number together, which they said was grievous. It was for Sirens...

The penalties take place in this way. He who is being punished is held... by his companions in a like cupidity, and is explored as to how much he inheres in it, and as to how much he has receded through the penalty; nor is he liberated from the penalty until he does recede, and becomes better...
Such is the penalty of hypocrites, and there is their Hell. (The pyramidal sack.)
How expeditiously penalties are inflicted, (Collisions, and breaking of the bones.)
Concerning a certain infernal penalty. (A magical Spirit is made pendulous.)
When the horror of the penalty prevails (over their delight), it is then the consummation (of evil Spirits).

The Sirens no longer cared for the penalties, but eluded them... But they were told that all penalties can be indefinitely aggravated, even so as to last for thousands of years... The more obstinate they are, the more grievous things they suffer...
She at last eluded all the penalties...
[A discourse] with Spirits, that they induce the penalty on themselves; and that the penalty is conjoined with the evil. Explained.
There are some who cannot be amended by any penalties, because they have imbued hatred, revenge, etc., from childhood, and have retained them to old age. (Their terrible condition in Hell.)
To (these gulfs in the extremes of each world) are sent those who cannot be mastered by penalties...

Hence other (infernals) who had also endeavoured to rise up, lamented... that if he wandered about free, they would run into his grievous penalties... Hence it is evident that they cannot rise up out of the Hells for fear of the penalty...
The judge (in Hell) adjudged them to undergo a penalty... He tolerated all things... provided they did no evil to anyone...
After many penalties, he at last suffered the last and hardest; but still in this penalty he said that he would rather die than desist from killing me.
All the penalties in the Hells are for no other cause, than that evils may be actually opened and known, and they are punished until they do not want them.

An evil Spirit cannot be withdrawn from evils, except by means of penalties. Cederstedt... wanted to withdraw himself from the evil, because he feared the penalty; but as the evil was in accordance with his nature, he could not withdraw himself... whereas when the penalty is being inflicted, he is so driven by the penalty that he does not want the evil... and then the Society in that evil is separated from him, but only until he is no longer in fear of the penalty. This is the reason there are penalties in the Spiritual World...

(The English lords) are punished with the penalty of tearing to pieces, which is one of the most grievous ones. They said that after [undergoing] the penalties they do not know whether their members cohere together; and they lie long in bed.

Reflection is given (an evil man after death) by means of many penalties, until, at last, they are averse to do evils, especially to the Societies where they have suffered. This reflection is external, and they are then kept in the Hells... They endure the penalties so long, and so grievously, that at last this reflection arises as it were of itself.

(These infernal) Spirits remain in the World of Spirits quite a long time... in order to tempt Spirits, and this until the measures of their evil are filled. Meanwhile, they endure many grievous penalties, but such that they are not completely deterred. At last, when their measures are being infilled, they endure more grievous, and, at last, the most grievous penalties, and this in quite a long series, on the way to Hell... At last, they are cast into Hell, so that they may there chastise and punish each other... and become such that they at once see penalties if they venture out... In this state they become more prudent, and see those in the World of Spirits...

This law (of doing to others as we would they should do unto us) is in Heaven... and thence every evil has with it a corresponding penalty, which is called the penalty of the evil; and it is in it as if it were conjoined with the evil. From this flows the penalty of retaliation. Explained.
To avert the evil of penalty, is contrary to order... Evil would increase until there was no good left.
He who is not the cause of the evil is not the cause of the penalty...
So those who do evils are driven by the penalties to reject them as of themselves. If they do not do so as of themselves, the penalties are not conducive to anything.
Infernal penalty in the same proportion. Signified, Explained... For all infernal torment, or penalty, corresponds exactly to the evils...

An evil Spirit is driven by penalties not to speak or do evil, and such he continues so long as he remains in the place where the penalty is floating before his mind; but as soon as the fear of the penalty recedes, he is evil as before.
Fears which compel the internals of man... relate, on the one side, to the penalties of Hell... But the fear of the penalties of Hell is external [fear] of the thought and will.
Evil does not recede through the compulsion which is effected through penalties; nor, afterwards, through the fear of them.
That... man is not reformed... through penalties. Explained.
By fears and penalties the external of the body is compelled, which consists in speaking and doing. This latter can be compelled... but the external of the spirit is not to be compelled...
While they were in externals, from the dread of infernal penalties. Signified.

With those not reformed, evils are removed through penalties... When an evil person undergoes penalties, as is the case in Hell, he is kept in them until it is perceived that, from himself, he does not want them... If he is not punished even to this intention and will, he remains in his evil. Nevertheless the evil is not extirpated...

After a time has passed, they are cast into Hell, when they are compelled not to do evils through penalties; but the penalties do not take away the will, intention, and derivative thought of evil; they take away only the acts.
